draft.title: A significant Hindu practice
card: A Hindu practice is something believers do that puts a belief into action. Practices differ across communities, and no single practice is followed by every Hindu.
Puja
worship of a deity, often at a home shrine or a mandir (temple). Offerings such as flowers, light and food express devotion and the belief that the divine can be present in an image.
Marriage
the wedding ceremony, often held around a sacred fire. It joins two people in the householder stage of life and expresses the duty of dharma within the family.
Pilgrimage
travel to a holy place such as Varanasi on the Ganges. Many Hindus bathe in the river there, as an act of devotion and in the hope of spiritual purification.
draft.remember: A practice is a belief acted out: puja shows devotion, marriage shows dharma, pilgrimage shows the search for purification.

a.q: Why is a Hindu wedding around a sacred fire called a practice that expresses belief?
opts: It acts out the duty of dharma within family life
It is required of every Hindu at the same age
It replaces the need for puja at a home shrine
It is mainly a legal contract with no religious meaning
a.why: The ceremony puts the belief in dharma and the householder stage into action. It is not followed by every Hindu in the same way, and it does not replace other practices such as puja.
a.clue: Think of what the ceremony shows about duty.

b.q: Priya travels from Sydney to Varanasi and bathes in the Ganges. Which belief does her pilgrimage most directly express?
opts: The river is sacred and can help purify a person
Every Hindu must make the journey once a year
Worship is valid only when done at a mandir
A household shrine has no religious value
b.why: Bathing in the Ganges at Varanasi expresses the belief that the sacred river can bring spiritual purification. The other options are tempting because they sound like rules, but the card says practices differ and none is followed by every Hindu.
b.clue: Focus on what the river means to those who bathe in it.

a.best: It acts out the duty of dharma within family life

b.best: The river is sacred and can help purify a person
